title: Eventual Consistency
description: Learn eventual consistency patterns for maintaining data accuracy across microservices.

data.text: Eventual consistency is the most common consistency model in microservices. Amazon, Netflix, and LinkedIn all rely on eventual consistency to achieve high availability and scale. Data may be temporarily inconsistent but will converge over time.

Eventual consistency guarantees that if no new updates are made, all accesses to the data will eventually return the last updated value. During updates, different replicas may temporarily show different values, but they will converge.

data.title: Implementation Strategies
items: Change data capture (CDC): Stream database changes to other services
Event-based synchronization: Publish events when data changes
Saga pattern: Compensate for failures with compensating transactions
Materialized views: Build denormalized read models from events

data.title: Amazon's Approach
data.text: Amazon uses eventual consistency extensively. Their shopping cart, recommendations, and search all use eventually consistent data. They accept temporary inconsistency for massive scalability.

data.title: Example: Eventual Consistency with Events
data.code: User updates their email. User Service publishes an event. Other services update their caches eventually.

# User Service
1. Update email in User DB
2. Publish UserUpdated event

# Notification Service (listens)
1. Receive UserUpdated event
2. Update email in Notification preferences cache

# Analytics Service (listens)
1. Receive UserUpdated event
2. Update user profile in analytics warehouse

# All services eventually converge to the same email

items.question: How long until data converges?
items.answer: It depends on your implementation. Event-based systems typically converge in milliseconds to seconds. Batch-based systems may take minutes or hours.

items.question: How do I handle conflicts?
items.answer: Use last-write-wins, version vectors, or conflict-free replicated data types (CRDTs). Choose based on your domain requirements.

items.question: Should I tell users about inconsistency?
items.answer: Yes, be transparent. Show a 'syncing' indicator when data is temporarily inconsistent. This manages user expectations.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Eventual consistency trades immediate accuracy for availability
Data converges over time through events or synchronization
Acceptable for many domains like social media and e-commerce
Use stronger consistency for critical operations like payments
data.takeaway: Eventual consistency enables scalable microservices; plan for temporary inconsistency in your UX.
